result.summary:
Read the full diff (git diff main...feature/WF02-REQ382-20260922) and the actual source of lib/letflow/routers/tenant_settings.ex, lib/letflow/identity/color_contrast.ex, lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex, lib/letflow/identity/tenant_settings.ex, lib/letflow/identity.ex, lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, and test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs (not just the design doc's description of them).

Invariant verdicts:
- INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES (S1 done, S2 migrations exist, per security-invariants.md's 2026-08-17 applicability note; this diff touches a tenant-scoped write path). PASS. (a) tenants row read (Identity.get_tenant/1, Repo.get(Tenant, id)) and write (Identity.update_tenant_settings/2, Repo.get_by(Tenant, slug: slug) + Repo.update) both correctly omit :prefix -- tenants lives in Postgres's default schema per Letflow.Identity's own 'Tenant administration' section comment (lib/letflow/identity.ex lines ~839-848), matching the existing Letflow.Routers.Tenants precedent exactly; no regression. (b) the audit-entry write (Letflow.Routers.TenantSettings.maybe_record_rejected_keys/5) IS :prefix-scoped: `prefix = Keyword.fetch!(conn.assigns.scoped_opts, :prefix)` (tenant_settings.ex line 127) -- sourced only from conn.assigns.scoped_opts, never a path/query/body value. (c) the audit entry's tenant_id field is derived from that resolved prefix via Letflow.Audit.insert_entry/3 -> TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) (audit.ex line 216), never accepted as a caller-supplied field. All three sub-checks confirmed by direct source read.
- INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) -- APPLIES (the API surface has materially existed since well before this diff, despite security-invariants.md's own stale 'S4 not started' reference for this invariant -- same kind of staleness INV-1's applicability note already had to correct once; treating this as checkable rather than deferring). PASS. Letflow.Routers.TenantSettings.settings_response_map/2 hand-builds `%{"tenant_id" => tenant.id, "settings" => updated_tenant.settings || %{}}` -- no raw %Tenant{} or Jason.Encoder-derived struct ever reaches the response; no other tenant field (slug, idp_realm_id, status, display_name) or rejected-key data is emitted.
- INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No Lua/WASM/scripting surface touched; S5 not started.
- INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES. PASS. No hardcoded secrets in the diff (grep for System.get_env/password/secret/token patterns across the changed files: no hits relevant to this diff). The audit-write failure log line (tenant_settings.ex lines 154-157) is `"tenant_settings.reject_unrecognized_keys audit write failed (tenant_id=#{tenant.id}): #{inspect(reason)}"` -- `reason` here is either `:not_found` (TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's failure atom) or an `%Ecto.Changeset{}` from Entry.changeset/2's own field-validation errors (audit.ex insert_entry/3) -- never a raw exception or connection-string-bearing term. Confirmed by reading Letflow.Audit.insert_entry/3's full body.
- INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. This route has no target-tenant path parameter and no lookup-by-ID of a foreign resource -- it always operates on `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`, the caller's own tenant (confirmed: no `:slug`/`:id` param anywhere in tenant_settings.ex's route or handlers). No cross-tenant probe surface exists on this endpoint at all.
- INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES (meta-invariant). Addressed by this review itself; see INV-1/INV-2/INV-4/INV-7/INV-8 verdicts above, each independently confirmed by source read, not by trusting the design doc's or ELIXIR-DEV's own claims.
- INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES. PASS. `grep -rn "Repo.query\|Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query"` across every new/changed file in this diff: zero hits. All queries go through Ecto.Query/Repo.get/Repo.update.
- INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES. PASS. Non-map request body: `handle_patch(conn)` fallback clause returns `Response.unprocessable/2` (tenant_settings.ex line 60-62), never crashes on a non-map JSON body. `:not_found` from Identity.get_tenant/1 and from Identity.update_tenant_settings/2 both handled via explicit case clauses -> `Response.internal_error/1` (defensive, since a token that already passed AuthPipeline/Authorize structurally can't hit this, same shape as Letflow.Routers.Tenants's own handle_promote/3 precedent). Changeset validation failure (WCAG-AA rejection etc.) handled -> `Response.unprocessable/2` with a traversed, plain-language message. Audit-write failure handled via explicit `{:error, reason}` case -> logged, `:ok` returned, does not crash or fail the HTTP response. `grep -n "^\s*{:ok, .*} = "` across the new/changed files: zero hits (no unguarded bare-match patterns).
- INV-9 (tenant-controlled outbound URL validation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. `logo_url` is validated for URL shape (URI.parse/1, http/https + host) but this diff never dispatches an outbound HTTP request to it or any other tenant-supplied URL -- it is stored/validated only.

Authorization correctness -- CONFIRMED CORRECT at the permission-matrix/runtime level, but the design's own coverage claim is FALSE (see FAIL reason below). `:TenantsManage` is PLATFORM_ADMIN-only: in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex, `role_allows?(:PLATFORM_ADMIN, _permission)` is the only clause returning true for `:TenantsManage` -- none of PROCESS_DESIGNER/PROCESS_OPERATOR/TASK_WORKER/AGENT_RUNNER/CANDIDATE's clauses list it. `endpoint_policy_key("PATCH", "/tenant/settings")` correctly resolves to `:TenantsManage` (authorization.ex line 590). `Letflow.Api.AuthorizedRouter`'s `__using__/1` macro (lib/letflow/api/authorized_router.ex) mounts `plug(:match)`, `plug(Letflow.Plugs.Authorize)`, `plug(:dispatch)` unconditionally for every router that `use`s it, including TenantSettings -- so the PATCH route IS genuinely enforced at request time regardless of any test-registration question. This part of the design's claim holds.

OQ-3 ruling (non-transactional audit write) -- ACCEPTABLE AS IMPLEMENTED, not a blocker. The settings write (the caller's actual requested mutation) commits first; the rejected-key audit entry is written as a separate, best-effort, sequential Repo call outside that transaction, logging-and-continuing on failure. This deliberately diverges from every other Ecto.Multi-wrapped audit write in lib/letflow/identity.ex (create_user/2, create_group/2, create_token/3, update_user_profile/3, update_user_status/3), but the divergence is justified here: (1) the audited event is a REJECTED-key notice, not the primary state change itself -- losing it on a rare transient DB error is a low-severity gap, not a compliance-critical record of an actual mutation; (2) wrapping it in the same transaction as the settings write would mean a transient, unrelated audit-subsystem hiccup could roll back and 500 an otherwise-valid, already-validated settings PATCH the caller explicitly requested -- a strictly worse failure mode for a PLATFORM_ADMIN-only, low-volume administrative endpoint than an occasionally-missing rejected-key audit trail; (3) the failure is not silent -- it is Logger.error'd with tenant_id for operator visibility. No numbered invariant (INV-1..INV-9) requires audit-write atomicity with the primary mutation. Ruling: acceptable, no rework required on this point.

FAIL reason: the design doc (lib/letflow/design/req382-tenant-branding-write-path.md, lines 583-587) explicitly claims 'this new router and its one authz_patch route are automatically covered by that existing mechanism [test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs]; no new test-infrastructure change is implied by this design.' This claim is FALSE. Read that test file directly: it does not scan lib/letflow/routers/ for every AuthorizedRouter user -- it walks an explicit, hardcoded `@routers` list (lines 48-77) and a matching `@mount_prefix` map (lines 95-110), both enumerating every OTHER router (Identity, Audit, Definitions, Instances, Onboarding, Tenants, Tasks, SolutionPacks, Promotions, Services, AdminServices, Entities, ExamSessions, Help) but NOT `Letflow.Routers.TenantSettings`. Confirmed via grep: zero occurrences of 'TenantSettings' anywhere in that test file. Consequence: the `for router <- @routers do ... test ... end` loop (line 153) never generates an assertion for this new router at all -- the policy-key-drift regression net every other authz_* router gets does not exist for this one. This is not a live authorization hole today (Letflow.Plugs.Authorize enforces :TenantsManage correctly at runtime regardless, confirmed above), but it is exactly the kind of 'design said it's covered, but it demonstrably isn't' gap this project's redundancy-based pipeline exists to catch before merge with no human backstop -- if a future change silently drifted or broke this route's endpoint_policy_key mapping, nothing in the test suite would catch it, unlike every sibling router. INV-6 requires this new data-access path to 'prove its scoping' to SECURITY-REVIEWER, not merely be asserted to; the design's own stated proof mechanism for this specific property does not exist.
issues: BLOCKER (authorization drift-detection coverage, not a live INV violation, but a false design claim requiring correction before merge per this pipeline's no-silent-gaps standard): test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs's @routers (line 48) and @mount_prefix (line 95) do not include Letflow.Routers.TenantSettings, contradicting the design doc's explicit claim (req382-tenant-branding-write-path.md lines 583-587) that the new router is 'automatically covered by that existing mechanism.' Fix: add `Letflow.Routers.TenantSettings` to @routers and `Letflow.Routers.TenantSettings => "/tenant/settings"` to @mount_prefix in test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs, re-run that test file to confirm it passes with the new router included (it should, since endpoint_policy_key("PATCH", "/tenant/settings") already correctly resolves to :TenantsManage -- this is a coverage fix, not a logic fix), and correct or remove the now-inaccurate 'no new test-infrastructure change is implied' claim in the design doc.
